# Independent audit: every feasible base moment is an actual cap

Audited `candidate 46f947c28385c3ea` in full.
Result: **PASS**; no correction identified.

The feasible mass/base-moment set is exactly the finite zonotope:
fiber masses determine these moments, and constant fiber densities
realize every box choice. A single continuous direction nonconstant
on every positive intrinsic affine fiber exists even when their
direction spaces differ. Its cap boundaries have zero H_q measure
on every positive fiber. The hinge gradient formula and continuity
therefore follow by dominated convergence with a uniform finite
fiber bound.

The bounded difference between the hinge and the zonotope support
function gives coercivity on the exact span U for every relative
interior target. Both the desired target and the gradient belong to
U, so vanishing restricted derivative is the full moment equality.
There is no unjustified full-dimensional assumption on the base or
on the zonotope in the redundant ambient coordinates.

For a relative-boundary target, a functional exposing its smallest
face fixes every nonzero-sign generating segment at the appropriate
endpoint. The zero-sign segments form precisely the translated
residual zonotope, and the residual target is in its relative
interior. The same hinge argument applies on its possibly smaller
span. A sufficiently large finite multiple of the exposing vector
then saturates all other fibers with strict margins. This handles
vertices, the zero target, and the full-mass target without a
limiting halfspace or boundary-mass selection.

For positive retained mass, some retained fiber has a point strictly
inside the cap because its intrinsic cap boundary is null. Interior
points of the original full-dimensional C approximate this point,
so C intersect H has nonempty ambient interior. Its mixed intrinsic
dimension remains exactly q and its intrinsic measure is precisely
the restricted source measure. When the base centroid is an integer
j, convexity places the full centroid in this actual subbody at
base j. Minkowski interpolation of the positive retained fiber
pieces also proves that the target fiber at j has positive q-volume;
the varying-direction case only increases the possible affine
dimension, which is bounded above by the original maximal q.

Finally, the finite retained-mass LP is compact and every maximizing
mass vector is realized by the single-cap theorem. Its stated LP
dual has the correct sign (a is unrestricted) and is not used to
assume geometric dual attainment. The q=0 exception is necessary,
and the stated counting example demonstrates it. No halfspace-depth
bound at the retained centroid follows merely from this result.
